# PM013: wip-limit-exceeded

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| family | PM |
| product | frob |
| severity (default) | warn |
| tier | universal |
| scope | repo |
| fix | manual |
| polarity | P+ |
| must_measure | false |
| version | 1 |
| since | 2.0.0 |

The repository has more tickets in progress than `[pm.wip] in_progress` allows.

Fires once, naming every holder, when the in-progress count exceeds the
limit. A limit of 0 turns the rule off. `work` and `start` refuse before
the limit is crossed, so this fires for tickets moved past the gate
(by hand, by a merge of two ledger branches, or by lowering the limit).

## Remedy

Finish or requeue one of the named holders with `frob requeue TICKET
--reason WHY`, or raise `[pm.wip] in_progress` in `frob.toml`.

## Examples

### PM013 WIP limit exceeded / Three in progress with limit 2 fires naming the holders #1 (line 10) (fire)

```text
limit 2
task a state=in_progress
task b state=in_progress
task c state=in_progress
```

### PM013 WIP limit exceeded / Two in progress with limit 2 is clean #2 (line 19) (clean)

```text
limit 2
task a state=in_progress
task b state=in_progress
```

### PM013 WIP limit exceeded / Tickets not in progress do not count #3 (line 27) (clean)

```text
limit 1
task a state=in_progress
task b
task c
```

### PM013 WIP limit exceeded / A limit of 0 is off #4 (line 36) (clean)

```text
limit 0
task a state=in_progress
task b state=in_progress
```
